svg.text: BORN, NOT MADE: THE CYCLE IN 12 STEPS, DOUBLE WALL

Side views, all at one scale. The robot is two bodies: a head and a tail. The head is a quilted double wall of silicone; every part but the arm sits between its two skins, and a shallow layer of gel lies on its floor.

The tail holds the arm. The arm prints the next head folded flat in the gel, and the newborn leaves through the mouth, full size. Then the tail prints a new tail and builds its arm, so heads and tails both reproduce.
tail, a hard clear print
arm, folded
brain, in the wall
head, quilted double wall
mouth
gel, a shallow layer
battery, pump, motor in the wall
wheels
The tail comes in
The tail, a hard clear print with the arm folded inside,
swims in toward the back of the head. Water and gel are in
from the start.
nine magnets in the tail face
steel discs in the head's cuff
the two gel faces meet
Dock by magnets
The tail docks from behind. Nine magnets in its face pull
the steel discs in the head's cuff, and the gel faces meet.
small electronic parts on the water
the arm lifts a part that floated in
Parts in through the mouth
The robot swims over the parts it wants until each floats
in through the mouth. The arm cannot reach out, so it lifts
them from the water inside.
next head, folded flat, 18 layers
a part set into a pocket of the new wall
print needle
Print the newborn head
The arm prints the next head folded flat in the gel, layer
by layer. At pauses it sets the parts into pockets in the
new wall; the next layers seal them.
keel, two tubes, fills first, 18 kPa
mouth end over the lip, cupped
ball needle in the rim valve
air line on the arm
“Birth”, keel first
The ball needle enters the valve at the rim. The keel fills
first and straightens the folds; the mouth end slides up
and over the lip.
push
sections open only past the lip, 6.3 kPa
the holder pushes the rim, 2 mm/s
Push and inflate
The holder pushes the rim while air goes into the cells
from the mouth end, so the newborn fills on the way out. A
folding crank carries the rim the last part.
backs away 60 mm on its wheels
newborn head, full size
its parts, in its own wall
Full size
The parent backs away and the newborn slides off the lip.
It leaves full size, the same head form, with its own parts
in its wall.
nose: pods for a cell and a pump
face: arm seat, magnet cuff
two segments, folded flat in the gel
Print a new tail
The arm prints a new tail in two segments, folded flat in
the gel. It sets a cell and a pump into the pods of the
nose and prints a seat for an arm into the face.
nose swims on its pump
face
they close on magnet cuffs
Out, and joined
The arm pushes each segment out through the mouth, where
air fills its quilt. The nose swims to the face and the two
close on their cuffs: a new tail, without an arm.
parent tail, free
the folded arm, built at its face
new tail waits, no arm
arm modules, a finite set
Build an arm
The parent tail lets go of the old head. A tail without gel
cannot print but can build: its arm picks four arm modules
and snaps each onto the last.
parent tail
new tail, face to face
the arm goes in base first, onto its seat
Hand over the arm
The two tails meet face to face. The new tail draws the arm
in base first; the arm stands up on its seat and unfolds.
new tail, made in the tank
gel line
newborn head
the next head, already in print
The newborn gives “birth” next
The new tail docks the newborn from behind and fills its
gel, and the cycle starts again. The parent tail docks a
head again: now two robots can give “birth”.
THE “BIRTH”, IN ORDER (STEPS 5 TO 7)

holder pushes the rim
air into the cells, mouth end first

rim fills, newborn out

5 min
6 min
7 min
Times from the double wall simulator. Before this,
the print takes about 12 hours and the silicone
cures for 16 hours in the gel. The newborn opens
only outside the lip, so it is full size as it leaves.
The new tail's segments are printed and pushed
out the same way, one after the other.
